attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack essay, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Almost certain' expresses near-certainty, which counts as high confidence, so it is a scored forecast. The proposition keeps the 'almost certain' wording. Modality 'will' slightly flattens it but is acceptable. No horizon is stated.

contract.note: The plain reading (lasting model availability plus broad, sustained exposure to AI misinformation) is the ordinary reading of 'overrun by a tidal wave'. It is not stretched either way. With no deadline, only a conclusive event can settle it.

evidence.note: April 2023 baseline of 49 AI content-farm sites. Most of them were not misinformation sites. It does not show society being overrun.

June 2026 tracker counts 3,749 AI content-farm sites. It shows growth in production, but it counts sites, not audience exposure or how much content is false. That falls short of the support condition.

OpenAI's account of itself (a company disclosure, not an independent finding). The influence operations it describes got little authentic engagement. This qualifies the exposure question but rules nothing out for the future.

reviews.rationale: This is a high-confidence forecast with no deadline. The evidence shows AI content farms growing and models staying available, but it does not show broad public exposure or a society-wide overrun. Nor is there any decisive event that would make the outcome impossible. The early-resolution rule is not met either way, so the claim stays unresolved.
